text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn spent a few hours in Dublin on Saturday for the closing day of the EU summit that brought together heads of state and government from both the 15 EU member states and those with association agreements and met Romanian President Emil Constantinescu.
- Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze intends to appoint Nograd County Police Chief Attila Berta to the top police post in Budapest.
- Gyorgy Giczy was re-elected as president of the Christian Democratic People's Party at a controversial weekend meeting of the national board, the legitimacy of which is already being challenged.
- The obligatory liability insurance fee for cars will cost 19.85 percent more on average next year, Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy announced Friday. (Sat.)

- Budapest police arrested one of their own late last week for selling top secret files on the investigation into the recent series of explosions and shootings to "three civilians" for HUF 50,000. (Sat.)
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Parliament will swear in two new cabinet ministers today, namely Mihaly Kokeny to head the Ministry of Health and Welfare and Frigyes Nagy to head the Ministry of Agriculture.

- The national board of the Young Democrats on Saturday confirmed its earlier resolution that it will prepare to contest the 1998 elections alone until it becomes clear what sort of cooperation is possible with other opposition parties.
- Czech Defence Minister Miroslav Vyborny will arrive in Budapest today for a four-day official visit.
- The Slovak-Hungarian joint venture Metaltrade Hungaria Kft won the purchase right for ore-treatment company Borsodi Ercelokeszito Mu at a competitive bidding.
- The new Museum of Contemporary Art opened its doors on Saturday, rendering Buda's Castle Hill one museum richer.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy will appoint Laszlo Kekesi as president of the Tax Authority. (Sat.)
- A total of $1.325 billion of foreign working capital flowed into the country through banks in the first nine months of this year, a study by the Ministry of Industry reveals.
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. yesterday decided to transfer 176,000 pieces of MOL shares to the 11 national ethnic minority councils and two other ethnic organisations.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Hungary's application for NATO membership was fortified by the shining performance of its IFOR contingent, Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti said late last week in Okucani, Croatia. (Sat.)
- Following a long decline, T-bill interest rates rose to 21-22 percent at the four auctions held last week.
- Eva Hegedus will resign as president of the Hungarian Investment and Development Bank effective January 1. (Sat.)

- Russian authorities detained an unspecified number Hungarocamion trucks on Friday, claiming that the trucks had not cleared their goods on entry, in the latest episode of an ongoing dispute that saw 56 Hungarocamion vehicles detained in Russia between January and August of this year. Managing director Mrs. Szakall said her company will refuse to deliver goods to Russia. (Sat.)
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The government is planning to take out a $200 million World Bank loan to help revamp the social insuirance system.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
